cards.subject: The tabernacle and its lamp, as an illuminated still life, seen straight from the front at eye level: a gilded tabernacle standing in the middle of an altar of white veined marble between the steps of its gradine, its low domed top crowned by a small cross, wholly covered by a veil of white silk (a conopaeum) that falls in soft folds to the altar and parts at the front to show a narrow strip of the gilded door and its small keyhole. Before it hangs, on three fine gilded chains from above, a sanctuary lamp: a gilded bowl holding a cup of ruby-red glass with a small steady flame, its glow falling on the silk, the gold and the marble. All else in soft shadow. Hushed, watchful, a presence kept. No figures.
cards.frame: instead of the arched window, a centred gold-edged QUATREFOIL medallion on a deep blue ground scattered with small gold stars, holding a single object like an illuminated still life; no halo, no figures
cards.basis: The tabernacle is 'irremovable', of 'solid and inviolable material that is not transparent', and locked, in a place 'truly noble, prominent, conspicuous, worthily decorated' (GIRM 314; can. 938). 'Near the tabernacle a special lamp, fueled by oil or wax, should shine permanently to indicate the presence of Christ and honor it' (GIRM 316; can. 940). Gilded metal is a traditional choice the norms allow; the red glass of the lamp is custom, not law. The excerpt is the lamp that burned before the ark in the sanctuary at Shiloh (1 Sam 3:3), the tabernacle's Old Testament type, from the First Reading of Wednesday of the First Week in Ordinary Time, Year II.

cards.subject: The altar crucifix and its candles, as an illuminated still life, seen from low down, looking up past the front edge of the altar and its white linen cloth: at the centre, standing on the gradine above the veiled tabernacle, a tall crucifix of dark carved wood bearing the carved corpus of Christ crucified in pale ivory, head bowed; on the gradine at either side three tall candlesticks of gilded brass, six in all, rising in height toward the cross, each holding a tall white beeswax candle with a lit flame. At the foot of the cross, leaning against the tabernacle, the centre altar card in a gilded frame, its print too small to read. The candlelight glows warm on the brass and on the ivory corpus; behind them hangs a dark wine-red damask. Night, solemn, recollected, the Passion kept before our eyes. No figures.
cards.frame: instead of the arched window, a centred gold-edged QUATREFOIL medallion on a deep blue ground scattered with small gold stars, holding a single object like an illuminated still life; no halo, no figures
cards.basis: 'On or next to the altar are to be placed candlesticks with lighted candles: at least two in any celebration, or even four or six, especially for a Sunday Mass'; 'on the altar or close to it, there is to be a cross adorned with a figure of Christ crucified' (GIRM 117), 'clearly visible to the assembled people' and kept near the altar even outside celebrations (GIRM 308); the candlesticks stand on the altar or around it (GIRM 307); the altar cross deserves every care (GIRM 350). The card takes the Sunday six, on the altar, rising toward the cross, a traditional arrangement the norms allow. The excerpt is 1 Cor 1:23-24, the Communion Antiphon of Saint John Chrysostom (13 September), from the Common of Doctors.

cards.subject: The Roman Missal, as an illuminated still life, seen from the side at three-quarters and a little above: a large, thick altar missal bound in dark brown leather with gilt corner-pieces, lying open on a low bookstand of gilded bronze at the epistle end of the altar, its cream pages showing no letters, its edges gilt. cards.subject: The chalice, alone, as an illuminated still life, seen in pure side profile at eye level: a tall chalice of silver-gilt, gold inside and out, with a wide plain bowl, a round knop set with small garnets on its stem, and a broad six-lobed foot engraved with a small cross. It stands empty and uncovered on a ledge of pale grey stone in a shallow niche, against soft silver-blue shadow; a single shaft of light from above catches its rim. Pure, precious, poised. No figures.
cards.frame: instead of the arched window, a centred gold-edged QUATREFOIL medallion on a deep blue ground scattered with small gold stars, holding a single object like an illuminated still life; no halo, no figures
cards.basis: The chalice and paten are 'held in special honor' among the sacred vessels (GIRM 327). Sacred vessels are 'made from precious metal' and, if of a metal less precious than gold, 'gilded on the inside' (GIRM 328); a chalice has 'a bowl of material that does not absorb liquids' (GIRM 330); glass, earthenware and clay are reprobated (Redemptionis Sacramentum 117). The form is left to the artist and regional custom (GIRM 332): the card takes a traditional silver-gilt chalice with knop and foot. The excerpt is the refrain of the Psalm at the Evening Mass of the Lord's Supper (1 Cor 10:16).

cards.subject: The paten, alone, as an illuminated still life, seen from directly above: a round, shallow paten of gleaming gold with a slightly raised rim and a small cross engraved near the rim, holding one large round white altar bread with a cross pressed into it. It lies on a dark polished walnut table, the grain warm and deep; low raking light from one side makes the gold glow and lets the bread cast a soft shadow. Simple, bright, a circle within a circle. No figures.
cards.frame: instead of the arched window, a centred gold-edged QUATREFOIL medallion on a deep blue ground scattered with small gold stars, holding a single object like an illuminated still life; no halo, no figures
cards.basis: The paten is, with the chalice, the vessel in which 'the bread and wine are offered and consecrated' (GIRM 327), of precious metal (GIRM 328); 'a large paten may fittingly be used' for the hosts of priest, ministers and faithful (GIRM 331); it is prepared on the credence table (GIRM 118c) and raised with the bread at the Preparation of the Gifts (the excerpt's rubric). The card shows a single large host, the traditional priest's paten; the bread is unconsecrated, before the Offertory.

cards.subject: The ciborium, as an illuminated still life, seen at three-quarters and a little from above: a gilded ciborium with a deep rounded cup on a tall stem and round foot, its domed lid, crowned with a small cross, lifted off and resting beside its foot, so that the cup shows itself filled with many small round white hosts; beside it lies its small veil of white silk, fringed in gold, folded back. It stands on a white linen cloth over a credence table of carved light oak, before a soft ivory wall in the pale gold light of late afternoon. Plentiful, gentle, bread for many. No figures.

cards.basis: Ciboria are prepared on the credence table, 'if needed', with the bread for the people (GIRM 118c); the priest distributes Communion from 'the paten or ciborium' (the excerpt's rubric; GIRM 160) and purifies it after Communion (GIRM 163). As a sacred vessel it is of precious metal, gilded inside (GIRM 328; Redemptionis Sacramentum 117); hosts are reserved 'in a pyx or small vessel' (can. 939). The covered cup on a stem with a cross on its lid is the traditional form; the lid is set aside so the hosts show.
